why_lead: Disney's 9 February results (known at this cutoff) are the cleanest new retail-facing catalyst: THR 'crushes Wall Street expectations, Disney+ nearly 130M subs' [[n0787]], Variety 'smashing growth forecasts' [[n0789]], Reuters 'streaming growth, park revenue boost shares' [[n0792]], Al Jazeera 'top estimates' [[n0791]], with fandom-media attention ([[n1189]], [[n1190]], [[n0726]]) and a simple repeatable story (Disney is not Netflix: NFLX -23.66% over 20 sessions). The card shows DIS at 147.23 USD (+3.33%) going into the report, against a risk-on tape (S&P 500 +1.45%, Nasdaq 100 +2.10%, VIX 19.96). Relation to earlier retail notes: Disney has not appeared in any earlier retail note or draft (2022-02-01 to 02-04, 02-07 to 02-09); Netflix appeared on 2022-02-01 only as a secondary 'follow the billionaires' item and is used here only as the contrast.
why_smaller: Chipotle: the pricing-power/inflation-winner narrative — +10.16% to 1,608.74 USD on record profit [[n0779]], menu prices about 10% higher [[n1164]], category-wide hikes [[n1177]]; new name, not in earlier notes.

Coca-Cola: the defensive dividend-bunker narrative — WSJ on investors gobbling up dividend stocks [[n0680]], KO +0.98% over 20 sessions versus Nasdaq 100 -4.97%, Investopedia [[n0775]], Morningstar energy-dividend competition [[n0876]]; pending results referred to only as 'next quarterly report'. Distinct from the 2022-02-02 Exxon 'Big Oil pays you to wait' item (different sector, defensive rather than commodity income).
Cameco: the energy-security/uranium narrative — McArthur River restart [[n0774]], CCJ +14.82%, URA +7.17%, Centrus +8.84%, Nord Stream backdrop [[n1304]]; new theme versus all earlier notes.
